advances: Actual planar convex geometry with two positively proportional limiting affine planes. The collapsing second cell carries no assumed interior source ball.

proof:
The second cell is $0\le u\le u_j^*=(\eta_{1j}-\eta_{2j})/(k-1)$ and the first is $u\ge u_j^*$. In the coordinates $(x,y)=(tv,t(1-v))$, $0\le v\le1$, area is $t\,dt\,dv$ and $M_j\to1/2$. For both branches the unscaled minimum is at least $u+\eta_{2j}$, and it converges to $t$ on $t>0$. The negative log tail is uniformly bounded in integral by a constant times $\int_0^\epsilon(-\log u)\,du$ on the portion $u\le\epsilon$. The positive logarithm is uniformly bounded. Thus the mean logarithm tends to $2\int_0^1t\log t\,dt=-1/2$ and $c_j\to c$. The inverse integrals before multiplying by $1/(M_jc_j)$ tend to $1+R_1$ on cell 1 and $(R_2-R_1)/k$ on cell 2. Indeed the primitive for branch $l u+\eta$ is $u/l+(a_j-\eta/l)\log(lu+\eta)/l$, and the common branch value at $u_j^*$ is $(k\eta_{1j}-\eta_{2j})/(k-1)$.

On a positive-rate level $L_j=e^{-jr}$ the exact density in $(v,r)$ is $jt/(M_j c_j l)$ with $l=1$ or $k$, by $|dt/dr|=jL_j/(c_jl)$. The rate ranges of the branches approach $(0,R_1)$ and $(R_1,R_2)$ on the positive axis. On every range $r\ge r_0>0$ the factor $jt$ tends uniformly to one on the feasible levels, since $|t-a_j|\le C(e^{-jr_0}+e^{-R_1j})$. It is uniformly bounded there, excluding positive endpoint atoms and giving the two densities by dominated convergence. The maximum rates tend to $R_2$. The bottom edge has length $\sqrt2 a_j$, rate tending to $R_2$, positive log $R_2j-\log c_j$ and normal $n_0$. Each coordinate edge has uniformly integrable logarithm by the same $u+\eta_{2j}$ lower bound with length element $du$. The top edge is bounded away from zero. This establishes the exterior formula and the needed compactness bounds.

The interface has length $\sqrt2(a_j+u_j^*)$ and parameter $c_j(k\eta_{1j}-\eta_{2j})/(k-1)$, so its positive-log mass tends to $\sqrt2R_1$ at rate $R_1$. Its outward normal is $n_0$ for cell 1 and $-n_0$ for cell 2, giving the two signed radial interface limits at the zero vertex. Multiplying the stated inverse densities by the anchor values gives the common positive measure $2t_o\delta_0$ on either side of the start. Multiplying by $M=1/2$ gives $t_o\delta_0$ throughout $(0,R_2)$, the radial uniform kernel of $t_oR_2\delta_{(0,R_2)}$.
statement:
Fix $k>1$ and $0<R_1<R_2$. Put $t=x+y$, $a_j=1/j$, $\eta_{\ell j}=e^{-R_\ell j}$ and $u=t-a_j$, and take
$$
K_j=\{x,y\ge0:a_j\le t\le1\},\qquad L_j=c_j\min\{u+\eta_{1j},ku+\eta_{2j}\},
$$
where $c_j$ gives volume-mean logarithm zero, $M_j=|K_j|$ and $r_j=(-\log L_j)_+/j$. These bodies and parameters satisfy the compactness hypotheses of the geometric rate theorem for large $j$. With $c=e^{1/2}$, the two affine planes converge to $ct,ckt$. The joint positive-rate inverse density of cell 1 is $(2/c)\delta_0$ for $0<r<R_1$ and zero otherwise. For cell 2 it is $(2/(ck))\delta_0$ for $R_1<r<R_2$ and zero otherwise. The fixed physical point is the zero vertex. The exterior positive-rate defect is $\sqrt2 R_2\delta_{(n_0,0,R_2)}$, with $n_0=-(1,1)/\sqrt2$.

For an interior anchor with $t_o=o_x+o_y$, the loss of cell 1 at $R_1$ and the birth of cell 2, weighted by their limiting anchor values $ct_o,ckt_o$, are both $2t_o\delta_0$, with no exterior atom at $R_1$. The oriented radial interface limits at that rate are $+t_oR_1\delta_{(0,R_1)}$ for cell 1 and its negative for cell 2.
title: An actual two-plane collar with exact nonzero phase compensation
